title: Flypaper effect assessment methods in the expansion of regional autonomy
author: Tanjung, Salam, et al.

steps.title: Assemble panel dataset
steps.instruction: Collect yearly data for each New Autonomous Region (NAR) required for the analysis, including General Allocation Funds (GAF), Local Government Expenditure (LGE), and Degree of Fiscal Autonomy (DFA). Structure the data as a balanced panel (cross‑section of NARs × time series of years) ready for STATA input.

steps.title: Conduct Chow test for model choice
steps.instruction: In STATA, run the Chow test on the full sample, the low‑DFA subsample, and the high‑DFA subsample to decide between Fixed‑Effect Model (FEM) and Pooled Least Squares (PLS). Record the probability values (F = 0.0000 for all three groups) and select FEM because each probability is smaller than the significance level α = 0.05.

substeps.instruction: Open the panel data file in STATA.
Execute the command for the Chow test on the whole dataset.
Repeat the test on the low‑DFA and high‑DFA subsets.
Note that F = 0.0000 for all groups; decision: FEM selected.

steps.title: Perform Hausman test to confirm model
steps.instruction: Run the Hausman test in STATA to compare FEM with Random‑Effect Model (REM) for the three groups. Record the chi‑square values (All Sample χ² = 0.0104, Low DFA χ² = 0.0393, High DFA χ² = 0.0085). Because each χ² probability is below α = 0.05, retain FEM as the preferred model.

substeps.instruction: In STATA, apply the Hausman command using the FEM and REM specifications.
Obtain χ² statistics for the whole sample, low DFA, and high DFA.
Compare each χ² probability to α = 0.05; all are smaller → FEM selected.

steps.title: Run classic assumption tests
steps.instruction: Check the FEM for heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. Use the t‑test for heteroscedasticity (All Sample t = 0.321, Low DFA t = 0.145, High DFA t = 0.422) – all > 0.05, so heteroscedasticity does not occur. Then perform the z‑test for autocorrelation (z = 0 for all groups) – probability = 0, which is < 0.05, indicating autocorrelation is present.

substeps.instruction: Execute the heteroscedasticity test (e.g., Breusch‑Pagan) and record t values.
Execute the autocorrelation test (e.g., Wooldridge test) and record z = 0.

steps.title: Apply GLS if autocorrelation detected
steps.instruction: Because autocorrelation is present, re‑estimate the FEM using Generalized Least Squares (GLS) in STATA to obtain BLUE‑compatible results. Verify that the GLS‑adjusted model no longer shows autocorrelation.

substeps.instruction: Run the GLS command on the FEM specification.
Check post‑GLS autocorrelation diagnostics; confirm autocorrelation is eliminated.

steps.title: Estimate final regression coefficients
steps.instruction: From the GLS‑corrected FEM, extract the regression coefficient for General Allocation Funds (β_GAF) and the coefficient for Local Government Revenue (β_OLGR) on Local Government Expenditure. Record these coefficients for each of the three groups (All Sample, Low DFA, High DFA).

steps.title: Assess Flypaper Effect presence
steps.instruction: Compare β_GAF to β_OLGR for each group. If β_GAF > β_OLGR, conclude that a Flypaper Effect exists for that group; otherwise, conclude that it does not exist. Document the decision for all samples, low‑DFA, and high‑DFA groups.
